reasoning_traces.think:
Ownership differentials between DraftKings and FanDuel reflect divergent user preferences and algorithmic weighting. The site-split ownership of Justin Herbert (~14% DK vs 21% FD) implies a 7% bias toward FanDuel users. This asymmetry is modeled via a differential operator ΔO_site = O_FanDuel − O_DraftKings, where the variance in ownership estimates reflects platform-specific behavioral clustering. Stack popularity, such as Burrow/Chase at ~30%, emerges from joint probability distributions of correlated players. The index S = Σ(O_i · W_i)/N captures the collective influence of high-value pairings. Platform bias B = max(O_FanDuel, O_DraftKings)/min(O_FanDuel, O_DraftKings) quantifies deviation from parity. These primitives form a dual framework: one for site-specific variance and another for inter-player correlation. Failure modes include overfitting to single-source models and ignoring dynamic shifts in player value. The epistemic risk lies in assuming static ownership patterns across evolving game states.
